member.name: T:TigerCS.Api.Controllers.CrmController
member.summary:
A thin passthrough onto Tiger CRM's read-only data-access port (ICrmGateway) — unit lookup by unit number, and the contacts/ owners/tenants/authorized representatives linked to a unit (MVP-API-Contracts.md §2.1-§2.3). This controller makes no verification decision of its own; it exists so an agent (or the verification-session flow below) has something to look up and select from. See CrmUnitLookupAppService's and VerificationSessionAppService's remarks for the full ownership boundary between Tiger CRM (read-only) and Tiger CS Ticketing (owns the verification decision).
Scoped to CS Agent/CS Supervisor only (PolicyNames.CustomerVerification) — not the contract's literal "Agent and above" wording, and not the global AuthenticatedStaff fallback. See PolicyNames.CustomerVerification's remarks for why: Solution-Analysis.md §4.1's Permission Matrix grants ticket-Create to only these two roles, and customer/requester verification exists solely to gate ticket creation. Reporting User, Department Employee, Department Head, CS Manager, GM, Chairman/CEO, and System Administrator are all denied — confirmed, not guessed.

member.name: M:TigerCS.Api.Controllers.CustomerLookupController.Search(System.Int64,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Search the intake's Department-configured source(s) — or all of CRM/PACT/Tasleeh if no Department was selected — for its phone number.
member.remarks: Always 200, with one entry per source actually searched — unsearched sources (because the intake's Department is not configured for them) have no entry at all, never a fake NotFound. A searched source that found nothing (NotFound) or could not be reached (Failed) never hides another source's match, and this call never blocks or gates ticket creation (POST /api/tickets). A Found source carries 0..N matched customers, each with 0..N units — pass whichever unit's unitReferenceId/contactReferenceId the agent selected straight to ticket creation to link it; PACT/Tasleeh matches are display-only (their units list is always empty).
member.param: The intake record whose phone number (and optional DepartmentId, to narrow which sources are searched) to search with.
member.response: Each source actually searched, one entry per source, each Found/NotFound/Failed.
No such intake record.

MVP-API-Contracts.md §5.2 / ISSUE-019. This is the only event that satisfies the First Response SLA — the automated acknowledgement never does, on any channel.
Write-once at the ticket level: a second call is answered with 409, because the target is measured against the *first* engagement and a later correction would silently move a contractual measurement.

Escalation is an independent dimension, not a status: an escalated ticket stays exactly as Open or InProgress as it was, and nothing here changes `ticketStatus`, resolves, or closes the ticket (ADR-0008/ADR-0011).
Levels only rise. A request for a level at or below the ticket's current one is answered with 422 rather than quietly de-escalating it.

member.summary:
The canonical Swagger/OpenAPI tag names for this API, plus the description shown next to each group in Swagger UI.
Tags are a documentation grouping only: they change nothing about routing, authorization, or behaviour. They are declared here (rather than as loose strings on each action) so that a tag is spelled exactly one way across every controller, and so can fix the order the groups appear in — Swagger UI otherwise sorts them alphabetically, which would interleave the intake/ticket flow with unrelated groups.

member.name: T:TigerCS.Api.OpenApi.TigerCsOpenApiOperationTransformer
member.summary:
Per-operation documentation: applies the [Tags] group an endpoint declares, and — for endpoints that are not [AllowAnonymous] — records that they require the Bearer scheme and can answer 401/403.
The 401/403 responses are not invented: Program.cs registers JWT bearer authentication and AddTigerCsAuthorizationPolicies sets a fallback policy requiring an authenticated, active employee, so every endpoint without [AllowAnonymous] can already return them. member.summary: The endpoint's declared tag group: the action method's own [Tags] if it has one, otherwise its controller's. Read directly off the action/controller rather than by scanning EndpointMetadata, so an action-level tag reliably wins over a controller-level one without depending on the order MVC happens to place attributes in that list. member.name: T:TigerCS.Api.OpenApi.TigerCsOpenApiSchemaTransformer
member.summary:
Keeps a schema's required list honest: a property whose type is nullable is dropped from it.
The generator derives required from a record's positional constructor, so every parameter lands there — including the optional ones. That contradicts what the endpoints actually accept: POST /api/intake-records, for instance, documents rawUnitNumberEntered as "must be omitted when isUnitRelated is false", and a client generated from an unadjusted document could not express that. Removing nullable properties from required leaves a statement that holds for both directions — a nullable field may be omitted from a request, and a client must not assume one is present.
Documentation only — model binding and validation are untouched.
